🇲🇽💳 <u>Banco del Bienestar launches a free, no-fee payments app</u>

The state-owned Banco del Bienestar presented its new mobile app at the mañanera. It lets users send transfers by card number, CLABE account or phone number, and pay or charge by QR code, all without commissions. It also shows balances and transactions instantly and finds the nearest branch. It serves the network that already reaches millions of social-program recipients, and the government made clear that cash will not be eliminated or banned.

🇲🇽🌳 <u>A reserve "created by the people, for the people": Semarnat wants to copy the Sierra Gorda model</u>

In Querétaro's Sierra Gorda Biosphere Reserve, companies pay communities to keep forests standing. Through the Carbono Biodiverso program, ejidos remove cattle, let the forest regrow, and use the money for patrols against illegal logging, road upkeep and local jobs. In 2025 it covered more than 40,000 hectares and 400 landholders and brought in 52 million pesos a year. Environment Secretary Alicia Bárcena toured the reserve and wants the model documented so it can be repeated elsewhere in Mexico.

🇲🇽🛡️ <u>Plan Michoacán, one year on: homicides down 42%, 1,657 explosive devices seized</u>

A year after Uruapan mayor Carlos Manzo was murdered, Mexico's federal security plan for Michoacán has cut intentional homicides in the state by 42%. Defense Secretary Ricardo Trevilla reports 1,657 improvised explosive devices seized. Army engineers armored loaders and graders to clear cartel-mined rural roads: 3,019 km covered in Apatzingán since June, and 36.3 km cleared in Cotija since October. Forces have mapped the routes that bring South American drugs through Michoacán's coast toward the US, and the cell behind Manzo's murder has been dismantled.

🇲🇽🏭 <u>Owners shut it down. Workers took it back.</u>

Grupo Porres closed the San Pedro sugar mill in Lerdo de Tejada, Veracruz, on August 5, saying it was no longer profitable. Three months later, on November 11, the workers walked back in and started maintenance for the harvest. A trust made up of workers, cane growers and a private partner now runs the mill. More than 700 direct jobs were saved, and the closure would have hit over 15,000 people in the Papaloapan basin. Governor Rocío Nahle: "This is a great achievement of the workers."
banner: SUGAR MILL: WORKERS REOPEN SAN PEDRO

🚨🇲🇽 <u>Trump threatens 50% tariffs over caravans. Sheinbaum: not one has reached the border.</u>

Trump threatened to raise tariffs on Mexico to 50% if it doesn't stop migrant caravans. Sheinbaum answered with the record: "Since President Trump took office, not a single migrant caravan has reached the northern border." About 10 caravans in two years, and once the INM tells people one by one that crossing isn't possible, most choose to go home and Mexico helps them do it. The one in Arriaga, Chiapas, started with about 600 people and is down to fewer than 100. Asked whether there would be repression, she said: "No."
banner: CARAVANS: ZERO REACHED THE US BORDER

🇲🇽🏭 <u>Mexican heavy-truck exports up 158.9% in October</u>

Mexico exported 13,518 heavy vehicles in October, up 158.9% from 5,221 a year earlier, according to INEGI. Production rose 129.6% to 16,375 units. January–October exports reached 111,912 units (+20.3%), and 93% went to the US. Even under Section 232 tariffs, the trucks that move North America are still made in Mexico. (El Economista)

🔥🇲🇽 <u>Honda fired him for organizing in 2011. Today he goes back in.</u>

José Luis Solorio was fired for union organizing at Honda's El Salto plant in Jalisco, then jailed on charges later proven false. The employer-controlled labor board took 15 years to rule in his favor. Honda filed an amparo to block his return, but the STPS set his reinstatement for November 12, 2026. Independent unions see it as a test of whether the post-2019 labor regime protects organizers once they're back on the shop floor.

🚨🇲🇽 <u>WikiLeaks cable: IFE official told the US Embassy the quick count could be withheld if AMLO lost by 3% or less</u>

A US Embassy cable published by La Jornada says IFE electoral councillor Arturo Sánchez Gutiérrez told American diplomats, 18 days before the 2006 vote, that the institute might not announce the quick count if López Obrador lost by 3 points or less. That is what happened on July 2. The embassy also wrote that he "clearly has little regard" for AMLO. Sheinbaum: the IFE has "at least one terrible stain, the 2006 electoral fraud," and now the opposition "is trying to discredit the 2027 election."

🇲🇽🏥 <u>IMSS-Bienestar: 118,000 health workers get permanent posts, 19,314 new hires</u>

Starting January 1, 2027, IMSS-Bienestar will give 118,038 health workers permanent positions, including 21,941 on temporary contracts "in precarious conditions." It will hire 19,314 specialists, nurses and residents, about 3,000 of them before November 30. Through Médicos por México, 78 mobile surgical teams will cover the system's 296 rural hospitals, with a target of more than 16,000 surgeries in 120 days. Five teams are already working in Chiapas.

🇲🇽🌎 <u>Foreign Minister Velasco heads to Tokyo as Mexico widens its map</u>

Foreign Minister Roberto Velasco is in Japan to meet Foreign Minister Toshimitsu Motegi, Japanese investors and Mexican scientists, and to launch the Mexican Chamber of Commerce in Japan. More than 1,600 Japanese companies already operate in Mexico, employing nearly 350,000 people. The trip comes days before Sheinbaum flies to APEC in Shenzhen.
